segments.text: When an AI processes your message, it converts words into tokens.
Each token starts as an embedding, a row of numbers.
As the network's layers process the text, they update those numbers based on context.
But those new numbers might not match the starting numbers for any token.
How can they still represent meaning?
An exact match isn't necessary.
The relationships between the numbers matter, too.
We can picture those relationships as positions on a map,
where nearby positions can represent similar meanings.
That's the idea behind vector space.
Let's look at how relationships work on a familiar map.
A map uses two numbers to describe position, latitude and longitude.
If we add Dallas to the map, it sits at 32.78 degrees north and 96.80 degrees west.
Next, we add Mountain View at 37 degrees north, 122 degrees west.
Then, we add New York City at 41 degrees north, 74 degrees west.
Now you get a set of coordinates that don't match one of our existing cities.
The first is 38 degrees north, 120 degrees west.
We can add that position to the map, marked with a diamond.
Which of our three cities is closest?
Mountain View is closest, even without an exact coordinate match.
Next, try a second new position at 40 degrees north, 76 degrees west.
Let's add this second diamond.
Which city is closest here?
The coordinates didn't match either city exactly,
but distance helped us find the closest match.
A geographical map uses two numbers to describe a position,
and comparing positions helps us find the closest match.
We can do the exact same thing with more than two numbers.
Imagine a taste test where you rate Coke, Pepsi, and hot coffee on seven characteristics.
Each drink gets seven numbers, called a vector.
Think of those numbers as coordinates that place the drink on a map.
We can't draw all seven dimensions,
but a simplified picture shows which drinks are closest.
Let's define Coke.
Its coordinates are Sweetness 9, Bitterness 1, Fizz 10,
Heat 2, Caffeine 3, Darkness 8, and Citrus 1.
This plot maps out those coordinates.
Next, Pepsi.
Sweetness 9, Bitterness 1, Fizz 10, Heat 2, Caffeine 3, Darkness 8, Citrus 10.
It sits near Coke.
Now hot coffee.
Sweetness 1, Bitterness 9, Fizz 0, Heat 9, Caffeine 8, Darkness 10, Citrus 0.
It sits in its own coffee and tea neighborhood.
Now you get numbers that don't perfectly match.
Let's add Mystery Drink A.
Its first six coordinates match Coke and Pepsi.
Compare the last number, Citrus.
Mystery A is 9, Coke is 1, Pepsi is 10.
Pepsi is closest, with a Citrus gap of only one.
Now add Mystery Drink B, Sweetness 2, Bitterness 8, Fizz 0, Heat 8, Caffeine 7, Darkness 9, Citrus 0.
Compare these with hot coffee.
Hot coffee is the closest match across all dimensions.
These numbers give each drink a position in vector space.
This is distance.
Smaller gaps mean closer positions.
You just found the closest match without needing an exact set of numbers.
AI applies this exact principle, but on a massive scale.
Its embeddings have thousands of dimensions, with values learned during training.
After the layers update a token's vector, it doesn't need to match another vector exactly.
Its position in vector space helps represent its meaning.
Let's read this sentence.
The tired cat sat on the mat during the May rainstorm.
It soon fell asleep.
On its own, the token IT could refer to many things.
But as AI processes the text, the layers update the numbers in ITS vector to carry information about its specific connection to CAT.
By changing those numbers, the system physically changes the token's position in vector space.
This visual meaning map shows how context changes that position.
The space groups concepts together.
Objects, weather, and animals.
IT starts at a position with numbers beginning 0.12 and minus 0.34.
Then the layers update the numbers.
The token travels along a path to its updated position, with numbers beginning 0.41 and 0.06.
IT remains a separate token, now near CAT.
Its new position reflects its connection to CAT in this sentence.
Meaning is a position in vector space.
Similar meanings usually sit close together.
